question.problem:
Consider the function $y=({x}^{2}+2x)^{6}\sqrt[3]{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}.$  The derivative of this function is given by

$$
{y}^{′}=\frac{({x}^{2}+2x)^{5}}{3\sqrt[3]{{sin}^{2}⁡x}}((ax+36)\operatorname{sin}⁡x+(b{x}^{2}+cx)\operatorname{cos}⁡x)
$$

Find the value of $a+b+c.$
question.worked_solution:
Our function can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =({x}^{2}+2x)^{6}\sqrt[3]{\operatorname{sin}⁡x} \\  & =({x}^{2}+2x)^{6}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{1/3}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides and use the product and power rules for logarithms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(({x}^{2}+2x)^{6}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{1/3}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(({x}^{2}+2x)^{6})+\operatorname{ln}⁡((\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{1/3}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =6\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+2x)+\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+2x)+\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =6\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+2x}\cdot (2x+2)+\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\cdot (\operatorname{cos}⁡x) \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\frac{12(x+1)}{{x}^{2}+2x}+\frac{\operatorname{cot}⁡x}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y(\frac{12(x+1)}{{x}^{2}+2x}+\frac{\operatorname{cot}⁡x}{3})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=({x}^{2}+2x)^{6}\sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =({x}^{2}+2x)^{6}\sqrt[3]{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}(\frac{12(x+1)}{{x}^{2}+2x}+\frac{\operatorname{cot}⁡x}{3}) \\  & =({x}^{2}+2x)^{6}\sqrt[3]{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}(\frac{12(x+1)}{{x}^{2}+2x}+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{3\operatorname{sin}⁡x}) \\  & =({x}^{2}+2x)^{6}\sqrt[3]{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}(\frac{36(x+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡x+({x}^{2}+2x)\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{3({x}^{2}+2x)\operatorname{sin}⁡x}) \\  & =\frac{({x}^{2}+2x)^{5}}{3\sqrt[3]{{sin}^{2}⁡x}}((36x+36)\operatorname{sin}⁡x+(1{x}^{2}+2x)\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
a+b+c=36+1+2=39.
$$
